topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic introduces the final course lecture and outlines its learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional cancer treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy alongside their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit specific cancer vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependency, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale and molecular mechanisms of oncogenic kinase inhibitors and how cancer cells evolve resistance, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how engineered monoclonal antibodies and cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugates are used to target tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss immune surveillance and modern methods to harness or engineer T cells to eradicate tumors using checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess ongoing clinical challenges, historical trends in survival, future management strategies, and the dilemmas associated with testing new therapies.
